title: The Sin We Thought We'd Left Behind

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now Abraham moved on from there into the region of the Negev and lived between Kadesh and Shur. For a while he stayed in Gerar, and there Abraham said of his wife Sarah, "She is my sister." Then Abimelek king of Gerar sent for Sarah and took her. - Gen 20:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
It is almost hard to believe. Abraham does it again. Years earlier, in Egypt, he had lied about Sarah being his sister to save his own skin, and it nearly cost him everything (Gen 12:10-20). Now, older, wiser, having walked with God through covenant and promise - he falls into the exact same sin. The old failure resurfaces as if he had learned nothing.

This is deeply humbling, and deeply honest. Scripture does not pretend that God's people outgrow all their weaknesses in a neat, upward line. Sometimes the very sin we thought we had left behind comes roaring back years later. The pattern we imagined we'd conquered proves to have deep roots.

If you have ever fallen again into a sin you were sure you'd defeated - an old fear, an old habit, an old compromise - you are not alone, and you are not uniquely broken. Even Abraham, the father of faith, stumbled twice over the same stone. Growth in grace is real, but it is rarely a straight line.

This should keep us humble and watchful. "So, if you think you are standing firm, be careful that you don't fall!" (1 Cor 10:12). But it should also drive us to Christ, whose grace covers not only our first failures but our repeated ones. Our hope was never in our own consistency, but in a Saviour who is faithful even when we are not (2 Tim 2:13).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is there an old sin or fear that keeps resurfacing in your life?
- Where do you need to stay humble and watchful rather than overconfident?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, I am humbled that even old failures can return. Keep me watchful and dependent on You. Thank You that Your grace covers not only my first sins but my repeated ones. Hold me steady in Christ.
Amen.
